---
title: "Titanic - Passenger Survival"
format:
  dashboard:
    theme: cosmo
execute:
  echo: false
  warning: false
  message: false
---

```{r}
#| label: setup
#| include: false
library(tidyverse)
library(plotly)
library(DT)

# The course data are saved in the same folder as this dashboard.
all_passengers <- read_csv("titanic_final.csv")

# Follow the template: keep passengers with a known age and port.
df <- all_passengers %>%
  drop_na(Age, Embarked) %>%
  mutate(
    Survived = factor(Survived, levels = c(0, 1), labels = c("No", "Yes")),
    Pclass = factor(Pclass, levels = c(1, 2, 3),
                    labels = c("First", "Second", "Third")),
    Sex = factor(Sex, levels = c("female", "male"),
                 labels = c("Female", "Male")),
    Embarked = factor(Embarked, levels = c("C", "Q", "S"),
                      labels = c("Cherbourg", "Queenstown", "Southampton"))
  )

class_summary <- df %>%
  group_by(Pclass) %>%
  summarise(passengers = n(), survival_rate = mean(Survived == "Yes"),
            .groups = "drop")

sex_summary <- df %>%
  group_by(Sex) %>%
  summarise(passengers = n(), survival_rate = mean(Survived == "Yes"),
            .groups = "drop")

theme_set(theme_minimal(base_size = 12))
survival_colors <- c("No" = "#E07A5F", "Yes" = "#3D7EA6")
```

# Overview

## {.sidebar}

This dashboard explores passenger characteristics and survival in the
course Titanic dataset.

**Included:** `r nrow(df)` passengers with a known age and embarkation port.

Use the pages across the top to explore the plots, search passenger
records, and read the findings. Hover over a plot to see details.

**Source:** [Course Titanic data](https://bryantstats.github.io/math421/data/titanic_final.csv)

## Column

### Row {height=25%}

```{r}
#| label: passenger-value-box
#| content: valuebox
#| title: "Passengers included"
list(icon = "people", color = "primary", value = nrow(df))
```

```{r}
#| label: survival-value-box
#| content: valuebox
#| title: "Survival rate"
list(icon = "life-preserver", color = "success",
     value = scales::percent(mean(df$Survived == "Yes"), accuracy = .1))
```

```{r}
#| label: age-value-box
#| content: valuebox
#| title: "Median age"
list(icon = "person", color = "info", value = median(df$Age))
```

### Row {height=75%}

```{r}
#| label: survival-by-class
#| title: "Survival by passenger class"
# Plot 1: Proportions make classes with different numbers of passengers comparable.
plot_class <- ggplot(df, aes(x = Pclass, fill = Survived)) +
  geom_bar(position = "fill") +
  scale_fill_manual(values = survival_colors) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::percent) +
  labs(x = "Passenger class", y = "Proportion", fill = "Survived") +
  theme(legend.position = "right")

ggplotly(plot_class)
```

```{r}
#| label: survival-by-sex
#| title: "Survival by sex"
# Plot 2: Compare the proportions who survived within each sex.
plot_sex <- ggplot(df, aes(x = Sex, fill = Survived)) +
  geom_bar(position = "fill") +
  scale_fill_manual(values = survival_colors) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::percent) +
  labs(x = "Sex", y = "Proportion", fill = "Survived") +
  theme(legend.position = "right")

ggplotly(plot_sex)
```

# Distributions

## Column {.tabset}

```{r}
#| label: age-distribution
#| title: "Age distribution"
# Plot 3: Density curves compare the shapes of the age distributions.
plot_age <- ggplot(df, aes(x = Age, color = Survived)) +
  geom_density(linewidth = 1) +
  scale_color_manual(values = survival_colors) +
  labs(x = "Age (years)", y = "Density", color = "Survived") +
  theme(legend.position = "right")

ggplotly(plot_age)
```

```{r}
#| label: fare-by-class
#| title: "Fare by class"
# Plot 4: Boxplots compare the median and spread of recorded fares.
plot_fare <- ggplot(df, aes(x = Pclass, y = Fare)) +
  geom_boxplot(fill = "steelblue", outlier.alpha = .4) +
  labs(x = "Passenger class", y = "Recorded fare")

ggplotly(plot_fare)
```

# Passenger Data

```{r}
#| label: searchable-passenger-table
#| title: "Passenger records - use Search to find a name or category"
passenger_table <- df %>%
  select(Name, Sex, Age, Pclass, Embarked, Fare, Survived) %>%
  rename(Class = Pclass, Port = Embarked)

datatable(
  passenger_table,
  rownames = FALSE,
  options = list(
    pageLength = 10,
    lengthMenu = c(10, 25, 50),
    paging = TRUE,
    searching = TRUE,
    dom = "lftip",
    scrollX = TRUE,
    language = list(
      info = "Showing _START_ to _END_ of _TOTAL_ passengers",
      infoFiltered = "(filtered from _MAX_ total passengers)"
    )
  )
) %>%
  formatRound("Fare", digits = 2)
```

# About

::: {.card title="Findings and data notes"}

![](logo.png){width=60 fig-alt="Titanic ship icon from the course dashboard template"}

**What the dashboard shows:** Among the included passengers, the survival
rate was `r scales::percent(sex_summary$survival_rate[sex_summary$Sex == "Female"], accuracy = .1)`
for females and
`r scales::percent(sex_summary$survival_rate[sex_summary$Sex == "Male"], accuracy = .1)`
for males. First-class passengers had a survival rate of
`r scales::percent(class_summary$survival_rate[class_summary$Pclass == "First"], accuracy = .1)`,
compared with
`r scales::percent(class_summary$survival_rate[class_summary$Pclass == "Third"], accuracy = .1)`
in third class. These are descriptive comparisons within this dataset.

**Cleaning:** The source file contains `r nrow(all_passengers)` passengers.
Following the professor's template, `r nrow(all_passengers) - nrow(df)`
records with missing age or embarkation port were removed. All plots,
value boxes, and table rows use the same `r nrow(df)` remaining passengers.
These results therefore describe this subset, rather than every passenger
aboard the Titanic. Fares are displayed as recorded in the course file.

**How to use it:** Overview contains the summary numbers and survival
charts. Distributions contains two plot tabs. Passenger Data provides
searching, sorting, and pagination. Everything runs in the browser after
rendering; this question uses a static Quarto dashboard.

**Source:** [Professor's Titanic dataset](https://bryantstats.github.io/math421/data/titanic_final.csv)

:::
